motion.name: route-introduction
motion.value: header, headline, supporting copy and diagram settle over about 1.4s; connectors then hand off through typed services to cloud workflows
motion.purpose: Give the first screen an authored route through Joshua’s engineering areas.

motion.name: reading-route
motion.value: 3px fixed teal line, transform scaled to document scroll progress in a requestAnimationFrame-throttled passive listener
motion.purpose: Show where the visitor is in the portfolio without interrupting reading.

motion.name: section-reveal
motion.value: one-time Intersection Observer entrance using opacity, transform and bounded clip-path; visible by default before hydration
motion.purpose: Mark the arrival of work, experience, skills and contact as the visitor moves through the page.

motion.name: diagram-resolution
motion.value: project diagrams settle their nodes and draw connectors after their row enters; experience and skill rules sweep once
motion.purpose: Connect the scroll motion to the systems-atlas visual language.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.value: mobile menu .24s; link arrows 3px over .18s; project border .28s
motion.purpose: Confirm interaction and focus without slowing navigation.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Keep content visible, remove entrance and scroll movement, and preserve clear color and focus feedback.

narrative.overview:
The portfolio reads like a clear map of connected engineering work. A cool mineral ground, deep teal type, route lines, and annotated diagrams make interfaces, services, and cloud workflows legible without posing conceptual illustrations as product screenshots. The writing and layout are direct, spacious, and technical without becoming a dashboard.

Inter carries the whole site. White panels and pale sea-glass fields organize evidence; a dark teal contact panel closes the route. The visual language is restrained enough for a hiring manager to scan, while the diagram grammar gives backend work a concrete form.
keyCharacteristics: A light mineral canvas with deep teal ink and one primary route accent.
Large, tightly spaced Inter headings beside concise supporting copy.
Bordered, rounded diagram panels with labels and captions that explain their conceptual status.
Clear keyboard focus, touch-sized links, and mobile diagrams that retain their sequence.

rules.name: The Labeled Diagram Rule
rules.body: A color shift may help distinguish a node, but each stage must keep a text label and the preview must say when it is conceptual.

rules.name: The One Typeface Rule
rules.body: Keep Inter as the visible type family across headings, controls, labels, and long-form text; use weight, size, and spacing for contrast.

rules.name: The Readable Route Rule
rules.body: Do not rely on a wide diagram to communicate the engineering story; maintain the same labeled sequence at narrow widths.

rules.name: The Tonal-First Rule
rules.body: Use surface contrast and thin borders before adding elevation; reserve shadows for overlays and a small number of featured sheets.

dos: **Do** use the mineral canvas, white surfaces, and deep teal ink as the default setting for new pages.
**Do** label every diagram stage and keep a caption when a visual is conceptual.
**Do** preserve the single-column sequence, touch targets, and visible focus treatment at phone widths.
**Do** use Lucide for interface icons and keep descriptive text beside them.
donts: **Don't** treat project diagrams or GitHub cards as screenshots of running products.
**Don't** add a second display font or an indiscriminate badge wall.
**Don't** animate essential content into visibility or require animation to understand a route.
**Don't** apply heavy shadows to ordinary project cards or skill chips.
